title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: a smooth complex-analytic space X (for Grothendieck, the compactified moduli space of curves with its boundary) with a normal crossings divisor D. X is cut into 'pieces' indexed by strata. D^*_{d_*} is an open stratum, indexed by a flag of codimension data d_* = (d_0, ..., d_r). Over it lies the normal bundle N_{d_*} (with dual or variant written Ň). Locally the normal crossings structure splits N into a product of line bundles. Removing the zero sections of these line bundles gives an open subset N^* ⊂ N (eq. 289). N^* is a torsor under a torus bundle, with fibres (C^*)^{d'_0 - d''_0}. On the previous page, (290) defined Ň^{d'_0}_{d_*,d''_0} as the inverse image of Ň^*_{d_*;(d'_0,d''_0)} under the linear projection (287) Ň_{d_*,d''_0} → Ň_{d_*;(d'_0,d''_0)}. By (291) it is an affine-bundle torsor (under a vector bundle) over Ň^*.

This page argues in three steps.
(292) The dissection piece V^{d'_0}_{d_*,d''_0} of X near the stratum is (heuristically) homeomorphic to Ň^{d'_0}_{d_*,d''_0} restricted to D^*_{d_*}. This is a linearization of a tubular neighbourhood: the piece is the part of the tube where a prescribed subset of normal coordinates is 'small but nonzero'.
(293) The projection Ň^{d'_0}_{d_*,d''_0} → Ň^*_{d_*;(d'_0,d''_0)} is an affine-bundle map, hence a homotopy equivalence.
(294, boxed) Composing gives a homotopy equivalence V^{d'_0}_{d_*,d''_0} ≃ Ň^*_{d_*;d'_0,d''_0} | D^*_{d_*}.

So each piece of the dissection has the homotopy type of a torus-bundle (product of C^*-bundles) over an open stratum. Grothendieck flags two caveats: there is no canonical map in either direction, and the statement is for now purely heuristic.

The next page turns this into a 'Scholie important': up to homotopy, the building blocks of the dissection of (X, D) are (C^*)^k-bundles over the open strata. This serves his programme of describing the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν}: understanding the homotopy type (and fundamental groupoid) of the neighbourhood of the boundary, piece by piece, for the Teichmüller tower.
errors: The key step (292) is explicitly heuristic. It needs a tubular-neighbourhood/linearization theorem compatible with the whole normal crossings stratification, i.e. a system of compatible tubes in the sense of Mather/Thom control data. This is true but not proved here; Grothendieck says so himself.

The equivalence in (294) is non-canonical. One can make it canonical by passing to the real oriented blow-up (Kato–Nakayama space), where the boundary pieces are honest torus (S^1)^k-bundles over strata. Grothendieck does not do this here.
Notation is inconsistent: Ň^*_{d_*;(d'_0,d''_0)} versus Ň^*_{d_*;d'_0,d''_0}, and the placement of the superscript * varies. This is harmless.

ideas.what: Pieces of the tubular dissection of a smooth space along a normal crossings divisor are homotopy equivalent to punctured normal bundles, i.e. (C^*)^k-torsor bundles, over the open strata
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy links of strata / deleted tubular neighbourhoods; boundary strata of the real oriented blow-up (Kato–Nakayama log space); Borel–Serre-type boundary for moduli spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom–Mather (stratified tubes); A'Campo (real blow-ups); Kato–Nakayama (1999); for moduli of curves, Harvey/Harer/Ivanov boundary and Looijenga's work
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the 'structure à l'infini' of M_{g,ν} and tubular neighbourhoods of boundary strata qualitatively; this precise formulation is not known to be published

ideas.what: Affine-bundle projection as a homotopy equivalence (293)
ideas.modern_name: Contractible-fibre bundle map is a homotopy equivalence

deep.surprise_reason: The page states the standard fact that boundary pieces of a normal crossings dissection have the homotopy type of torus bundles over strata. It is explicitly heuristic and is well known through the theory of stratified tubes and real oriented blow-ups. It is historically interesting as part of Grothendieck's unpublished working-out of the 'structure à l'infini' programme, but it contains nothing new mathematically.
transcription_corrections: The first line reads 'Je dis qu'on a donc une [-équivalence-] "homéomorphisme"' with '(heuristique!)' below; the struck word is 'équivalence'.
The line after (293), 'qui est une équivalence d'homotopie', is wavy-underlined. The following line 'une équivalence d'homotopie' introduces (294), as in 'd'où une équivalence d'homotopie'.

Final text: 'qui a le seul inconvénient de ne pas correspondre à une flèche canonique dans un sens ni dans l'autre, et (pour le moment) d'avoir une valeur purement heuristique. Retenons cependant la' — the connective is likely 'et' rather than 'mais'.
